stack_check.build: prisma migrate deploy && prisma db seed && next build

c-1-1.check: GET /api/skus returns 200 with a JSON array of SKU with length 8

c-1-2.check: sc-skus-list renders exactly 8 elements with data-testid=sku-row

c-2-1.check: GET /api/reorder-suggestions returns 200 with Suggestion[] where for every item qty_to_order == max(0, reorder_point - on_hand)

c-2-2.check: sc-suggestions renders one data-testid=suggestion-row per item where qty_to_order > 0, and none where qty_to_order == 0

c-2-3.check: Each rendered suggestion row shows its qty_to_order in a cell with data-testid=qty-to-order

c-3-1.check: POST /api/purchase-orders with lines [{sku_id, qty}] returns 200 with JSON { id: number, itemsCount: number, totalQty: number }

c-3-2.check: sc-suggestions renders a button with data-testid=po-submit whose text includes '(2)' after two rows are checked

c-3-3.check: After selecting rows and clicking Create Purchase Order, the app navigates to /purchase-orders/created?items=<n>&total=<m>

c-3-4.check: sc-po-created renders the two numbers from the URL (data-testid=po-created-items and data-testid=po-created-total)

c-4-1.check: GET /api/purchase-orders returns 200 with an array of { id, itemsCount, totalQty }

c-4-2.check: sc-po-history renders one data-testid=po-row per order and shows both itemsCount and totalQty on each row

c-4-3.check: GET /api/purchase-orders/:id returns 200 with { id, lines: [{ sku_id, name, qty }], itemsCount, totalQty }

c-4-4.check: sc-po-detail renders one data-testid=po-line per line, each showing a SKU name and qty
